actions.name: Post job ads on professional networking platforms and online hiring and freelance gig work websites
actions.description: Recruiters post job ads on professional networking platforms and online hiring and freelance “gig work” websites like LinkedIn, Indeed, and Upwork.

actions.name: Rank resumes based on likelihood of access to sensitive information
actions.description: Resumes are ranked based on likelihood of access to sensitive information; recruiters begin their contact strategies.

actions.name: Conduct virtual interviews while concealing recruiter identity
actions.description: When interviews are required, they are held virtually. Recruiters conceal their identity and may start probing applicants about access to government contacts.

actions.name: Ask military members about their roles and unit activities during interviews
actions.description: Military members may be asked about their roles and unit activities, home base or naval vessel during interviews.

actions.name: Request candidates to write trial reports on topics related to China and defense
actions.description: Candidates are asked to write a trial report on a topic such as China’s bilateral relations, the Indo-Pacific region, related defense issues, or international trade.

actions.name: Inform recruits that additional reports require more privileged information and shift conversation to encrypted messaging
actions.description: Recruits are informed that for additional reports, the client requires more privileged information. At some point, intelligence officers typically move the conversation to a more secure platform, such as encrypted messaging applications.

actions.name: Pay recruits for reports using various payment methods
actions.description: Recruits receive anywhere from a few hundred to several thousand dollars per report, and may be offered more money in return for increasingly sensitive information. Payment methods include third-party payment platforms such as PayPal, Payoneer, Zelle, Skrill, Wise, Western Union, e-transfer, and cryptocurrency.

actions.name: Pose as employees of private consultancies, think tanks or HR firms representing fake cover companies
actions.description: Chinese intelligence officers or their affiliates pose as employees of private consultancies, think tanks or human resources (HR) firms, and place online job advertisements for foreign policy and defense analysts or similar roles. They represent fake, but often legitimate-looking, cover companies and claim to be located in countries other than China.
